content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a hyperspectral image reconstruction method for coded aperture snapshot spectral imager. The idea is to use spatial-spectral transformer to handle the entangled data loss, and use a mask-aware learning strategy to handle the masked data loss, where both losses were generated from the physical process when the image was generated. The experiments were conducted on two public datasets, with an ablation study. The results show that the proposed method outperforms several recently published methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

- Reconstruction for coded aperture snapshot spectral imager is an active research topic in hyperspectral image generation and processing.
- The proposed method targets two problems introduced in the image generation process.
- The proposed method is effective and shows promising results on two datasets.

Cons:

- The novelty of the paper is not significant. First, many hyperspectral image reconstruction/classification papers have used transformers to explore the global attention mechanism in hyperspectral images, e.g. "Coarse-to-Fine Sparse Transformer for Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction", "Hyperspectral Image Denoising Based on Parallel Cross-Fusion Network", and "Spectral–Spatial Transformer Network for Hyperspectral Image Classification: A Factorized Architecture Search Framework". Second, the mask-aware learning idea is not new either, e.g. "Mask-guided spectral-wise transformer for efficient hyperspectral image reconstruction", "Gap-net for snapshot compressive imaging", "End-to-end low cost compressive spectral imaging with spatial-spectral self-attention", "Self-supervised neural networks for spectral snapshot compressive imaging", and "A new backbone for hyperspectral image reconstruction". Therefore, the two novel contributions of this paper can only be considered incremental.

- I am not convinced that the parallel spatial-spectral attention fusion method can fully capture the spectral-spatial relationship in hyperspectral images. The method still treats spatial attention and spectral attention separately. 

- It is understandable that two attentions are better than one. However, the mechanism of why parallel attention fusion is better than sequential fusion has not been convincingly justified. The results in the ablation study show a slight difference, but the results were obtained on two small datasets that do not cover a wide range of scenarios.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The problem and methods are clearly presented. However, as mentioned above in the weakness part, the originality and novelty of this paper is not significant. The method is not easy to implement as many details are missing.
content.summary_of_the_review: This is a well-written paper. The proposed method is effective. The contribution of the work is implemental from the hyperspectral image reconstruction and from the learning representation point of view.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper aims to develop software to reconstruct a 3D hyperspectral image from the 2D image encoded by the coded aperture snapshot spectral imager (CASSI). The authors claim the two challenges: (1) CASSI compresses the information of multiple wavelengths to a single 2D measurement by channel-wise entangling and addition (implemented by a disperser), which leads to entangled data loss. (2) CASSI blocks the light with a physical binary mask for signal encoding, yielding the masked data loss upon some pixels. The authors propose a spatial-spectral (S2-) transformer architecture with a mask-aware learning strategy. The authors present some comparisons with existing methods using some public datasets. They conclude that their model achieved promising performance quantitatively and perceptually.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strength:
+ The code seems to be open to the public. It contributes to reproducibility.
+ PSNR and SSIM achieved the best among compared methods.
# Weaknesses:
+ The contributions are unclear. 
+ This paper has many issues with technical writing and English. Reading this paper requires a lot of labor.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
+ Some statements are NOT convincing. The authors should elaborate on them for clarification.
  + "by observation" in section 3.2 and section 4.2.
  + "fails to disassemble the spatial and spectral clues,"
  + "However, it fails to describe the spectral variations in each head. Besides, manually dividing the embedding into T heads is quite inflexible."
+ Applying different attention mechanisms on spatial and spectral dimensions is not new as the TSA-Net did. The authors should address the related work more carefully to clarify the technical issues that the authors solved.
+ Authors fail to differentiate notations. For example, the authors referred to Z as input and output in eqs 6, 10, and 11. The authors probably wrote down the equations like programming and used Z for temporary variables. However, this is NOT understandable for the readers. I could not follow the equations in detail. 
+ The motivation and effect of the mask-aware learning strategy are not clear enough. As far as I understood, this idea corresponds to the term of MA in eq 13, but not explained well how the authors designed it. Moreover, as presented in Table 3b, including MA without pre-train degrades the results. It is also necessary to show the result with pre-train without MA to support the contribution of the mask-aware learning strategy.
+ The paper sections are not well-organized. For example, the author introduces linear projection and defines it later in section 3.3.
content.summary_of_the_review: As raised above, this paper has many issues to be accepted.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors propose spatial and spectral attention for hyperspectral image reconstruction. They also introduced a mask-aware loss. 
I don't think mathematical expressions for the proposed approach are rigorous. Then, it is very difficult to follow the proposed approach.
They provide ablation studies to validate spatial and spectral attention.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Spatial and spectral attention.
The tokens defined just before Eq. (6) already include spatial and spectral information. In that sense, I could not get the difference between spatial attention and spectral attention.
To my understanding, Q and K in Eqs. (8) and (9) are 3rd-order tensors. The transpose operation for the 3rd-order tensors is not well defined in this paper.


Masked-Aware Loss
Eqs. (12) and (13) may not be rigorous. I could not get what i represents. Does it represent a stage or a multi-head?
Those equations may miss summation. 
This paper does not include sufficient discussion why the feature map should be similar to the masked input.

I could not get the meaning of Fig. 5. F and F' should be 3rd-order tensors. In addition, the block diagram at the top of the figure is ambiguous.

Minor comment
In Eqs. (1) and (3), they used the same symbol for a different meaning.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
As mentioned in strangeness and weakness, I don't think the clarity of this paper is good enough due to the lack of mathematical rigorousness.
I guess main idea of the proposed spatial and spectral attention is basically the same as MLP mixer. The paper missed to cite the papers related to the MLP mixer and associated discussion.
content.summary_of_the_review:
As mentioned in strangeness and weakness, I don't think the clarity of this paper is good enough due to the lack of mathematical rigor.
Even if the performance of the proposed algorithm is better than existing algorithm, the authors should explain clearly and rigorously.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
Regarding hyperspectral CASSI imaging reconstruction, this paper proposed two kinds of information loss, that is, (i) To obtain
2D measurements, CASSI dislocates multiple channels by disperser-titling and squeezes them onto the same spatial region, yielding an entangled data loss. (ii) The physical coded aperture (mask) will lead to a masked data loss by selectively blocking the pixel-wise light exposure. Referring to the data loss, this paper introduced a spatial-spectral attention block; regarding the second loss, this paper proposed the mask-aware loss function.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
1. The analysis of hyperspectral imaging reconstruction information loss is interesting, whereas the authors provide two efficient way to reconstruct the lost information.
2. The experimental results demonstrates the advantage of proposed method.
3. The spatial-spectral attention/transformer architectures have been widely utilized for hyperspectral processing, but the related analysis is insufficient.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Novelty: the explaination of reconstruction loss is interesting. The proposed spatial-spectral transformer architecture is also proved efficient in the experimental section. But the review of the related spatial-spectral attention block is insufficient.
content.summary_of_the_review: Spatial-spectral exploration for hypersepctral processing is popular and have been widely studied, both from model-based methods and learning based methods. The review of related works can be enhanced. Furthermore, the performance of proposed method is of great advantage, but where the advantage comes from? Can the proposed module (mask-aware attention) be utilized to other methods to improve the accuracy? How to generate the core novelty from the proposed method still remains a problem

content.title: S^2-Transformer for Mask-Aware Hyperspectral Image Reconstruction
content.abstract: The technology of hyperspectral imaging (HSI) records the visual information upon long-range-distributed spectral wavelengths. A representative hyperspectral image acquisition procedure conducts a 3D-to-2D encoding by the coded aperture snapshot spectral imager (CASSI), and requires a software decoder for the 3D signal reconstruction. By observing this physical encoding procedure, two major challenges may stand in the way of a high-fidelity reconstruction: (i) To obtain 2D measurements, CASSI dislocates multiple channels by disperser-titling and squeezes them onto the same spatial region, yielding an entangled data loss. (ii) The physical coded aperture (mask) will lead to a masked data loss by selectively blocking the pixel-wise light exposure. To tackle these challenges, we propose a spatial-spectral (S2-) transformer architecture with a mask-aware learning strat- egy. Firstly, we simultaneously leverage spatial and spectral attention modelings to disentangle the blended information in the 2D measurement along both two dimensions. A series of Transformer structures across spatial & spectral clues are systematically designed, which considers the information inter-dependency between the two-fold cues. Secondly, the masked pixels will induce higher predic- tion difficulty and should be treated differently from unmasked ones. Thereby, we adaptively prioritize the loss penalty attributing to the mask structure by inferring the difficulty-level upon the mask-aware prediction. Our proposed method not only sets a new state-of-the-art quantitatively, but also yields a better perceptual quality upon structured areas. Code and pre-trained models are available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/S2-transformer-HSI-FEBF.
